observations: Photos 0 and 1 show the soleplate from above and below; it has multiple steam holes and no visible deep scratches or burn marks, but image is slightly blurred for fine scratch detail.
Photo 2 shows the top of the iron with a green/white body, a steam dial (positions 1-4), a spray button, and a visible 'PHILIPS' wordmark near the front.
Photo 3 shows the side profile with the brand 'PHILIPS' and a secondary logo that appears to read 'ELANCE' near the heel, along with a translucent green water tank and a round temperature dial.
Power cord is coiled and visible in photos 2 and 3; insulation looks intact in the visible sections but the plug end and full cord length are not shown.
No photo shows the iron powered on, steaming, or any indicator light lit.
Watermarks 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'BEN' overlay the images but do not obscure key identifying features.

read_from: photo 3 side view - PHILIPS and partial ELANCE text

claims.evidence: No photo or video shows the iron powered on, heating, or producing steam.
Soleplate photos (0,1) show no obvious damage but resolution is insufficient to confirm absence of scratches or scale buildup; body photos (2,3) show normal wear consistent with used item.
No origin marking, import sticker, or voltage plate is visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Iron may not heat or may have a faulty thermostat/element
risks.proof: A short video clip showing the iron plugged in, heating indicator light on, and steam being produced

risks.risk: Soleplate could have hidden scratches, pitting, or residue affecting fabric contact
risks.proof: Close-up, well-lit photo of the entire soleplate at an angle that shows surface texture clearly

risks.risk: Power cord could be frayed or damaged near the plug, a common safety issue in used irons
risks.proof: Clear photo of the full cord length including the plug end
risks.if_unproven: priced as cord condition unknown/risk of replacement needed

risks.risk: Water tank or steam vents could be clogged with mineral scale affecting steam output
risks.proof: Photo or video of water being poured in and steam/spray function demonstrated

risks.risk: Voltage/plug type may not match local Nigerian standard sockets if truly 'foreign used'
risks.proof: Clear photo of the plug type and any voltage rating plate on the iron
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible plug adapter needed

proof_requests: Video of the iron plugged in and heating up with steam being produced
Clear, well-lit close-up of the entire soleplate surface
Photo of the full power cord and plug
Photo of the voltage/rating plate on the iron body
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used Philips steam iron, but the seller's 'working very well' and 'good condition' claims are unverifiable from static photos alone, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-demonstrated, unverified-condition used iron pending a heating/steam video and closer soleplate and cord shots.
